# Load more: `jl-load-more`

The end of a long list: how much shows, and a button for the next page.

- Class `JlLoadMore`, a molecule: `import { JlLoadMore } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/load-more

The end of a long list read a page at a time, as the collections pattern lays it out: how much of the
list shows ("30 of 120") and a Show more button that asks for the next page with more. The page sets shown and total
as pages come, and loading while one is on its way; the element takes no room once the whole list shows. Both texts
can be set, for pages in other languages.

## Use

```ts
import { JlLoadMore } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlLoadMore shown={30} total={120} />
```

```html
<jl-load-more shown="30" total="120"></jl-load-more>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `shown` (attribute `shown`): `number`, default `0`. How many items the list shows.
- `total` (attribute `total`): `number`, default `0`. How many it has in all; once they all show, the element takes no room.
- `loading` (attribute `loading`): `boolean`, default `false`. The next page is on its way: the button shows a spinner and ignores presses.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. The button's text. Empty: jlib's own text, in the language shown.
- `countText` (attribute `count-text`): `string`, default `''`. What shows beside the button; {shown} and {total} are filled. Empty: jlib's own text, in the language shown.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `more` (`onMore` in JSX), detail `undefined`: People asked for the next page.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The row of the count and the button.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### A page at a time

Under a list: each press brings 30 more, until the 120 show.

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <ul class="demo-items" style="margin: 0; padding-left: 20px; max-height: 160px; overflow: auto"></ul>
  <jl-load-more class="demo-more"></jl-load-more>
</div>
```

```js
const more = root.querySelector('jl-load-more');
more.total.set(120);
more.events.register('more', async () => {
  more.loading.set(true);
  const page = await fetchPage(more.shown.get());
  list.append(...page);
  more.shown.set(more.shown.get() + page.length);
  more.loading.set(false);
});
```

### Other words

Texts of another language.

```html
<jl-load-more shown="50" total="1204" label="Afficher plus" count-text="{shown} sur {total}"></jl-load-more>
```
